scope: Read-only GPAW 26.7.0 plane-wave slab/dipole source audit and interpretation of existing verified AgSi off/on archives. No DFT, calculator, MPI, gap-manifest, or input changes.

references.finding: Forwards Atoms.pbc to the uniform grid and passes configured Poisson parameters, including dipolelayer, to make_poisson_solver.
For mode='pw', realspace is false and zerobc is false on all axes; UGDesc still receives the pbc metadata.
PWDesc initializes its Domain with (True, True, True), independent of Atoms.pbc.
Builds PWPoissonSolver and wraps it when dipolelayer is truthy; the 'xy' string is not decoded as an axis in this new PW path.
Uses reciprocal-space PW kinetic energies as the periodic Coulomb kernel denominator and sets the G=0 potential component to zero.
Requires exactly two periodic grid directions, infers the correction axis from the nonperiodic direction, and adds a sawtooth potential and dipole energy term.
Legacy DipoleCorrection documents and parses plane strings such as 'xy', then requires a nonperiodic correction direction. This differs from the new PW wrapper's axis inference.
The installed dipole test constructs GPAW with mode='lcao'; it does not establish coverage of the new plane-wave Poisson backend.

interpretation: In the new PW path, slab pbc metadata does not create open-z or Coulomb-truncated electrostatics: the PW basis and reciprocal Poisson kernel remain three-dimensionally periodic; the dipole layer applies a correction along the inferred nonperiodic grid axis.

The original-vacuum AgSi off/on pair demonstrates a small correction delta for this exact fixed-ion geometry only; its large residual forces and different cell do not prove relaxed behavior or 26-A vacuum convergence.
minimum_control_recommendation: Keep PBC and dipole setting fixed across the registered separation scan; record PBC, Poisson parameters, and native/free energy conventions on every point.

To isolate dipole-correction sensitivity at the exact 26-A geometry, compare a matched same-coordinate/same-cell OFF/ON pair; if the registered ON parent already exists, add only the same-cell OFF control after A authorizes it.
To test 26-A vacuum-size adequacy, compare the same slab geometry and same dipole setting at 26 A and one larger-z cell, changing only cell height. OFF/ON alone cannot establish vacuum convergence.
To separate both effects, use the 26-A ON parent, one same-cell OFF control, and one larger-cell ON control. Keep the registered entries disabled until A decides.
limitations: No electronic-structure calculation or runtime solver test was performed in this audit.
The installed dipole test cited above uses LCAO and is not a PW-backend test.
The matched archive pair is one original-vacuum geometry, not a 26-A vacuum convergence study or a relaxed structure.
